# About this appendix {.unnumbered}

This online appendix accompanies *Social Security Design and Its Political Support* by Rasmus K. S. Berg and
Martín Gonzalez-Eiras. It holds the tables and figures behind the paper's quantitative sections, the robustness checks
that the paper's appendix G summarizes in one figure, and the numerical checks behind its results, with each figure set beside the
tables that print its numbers. Every exhibit is built by the paper's own pipeline from the model's results, so the
numbers are the paper's to the last printed digit; [replication](replication.qmd) lists where each one comes from.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
**Reading an exhibit.** Point at a marker of a figure to read its value; click it to bring up the table that prints
it, with its row highlighted. Point at a table row to find its markers in the figure. Where an exhibit exists under
both calibrations of the households' taste for leisure, a switch moves between the paper's calibration, common
$X$, and the alternative, vector $X_i$ ([OA.3.2](oecd.qmd#oecd-vectorx)), and *mark the cells that differ* shows
which numbers the choice moves. The address in the browser keeps the selection, so a link opens the same table
and row. Under *Source*, each exhibit lists the files it reads, with downloads, the builder that makes it and the
command that rebuilds it. A grey badge marks an exhibit of the paper itself; every other exhibit is numbered here,
Table or Figure OA.*k*.

The print edition, a PDF under the download link of the sidebar, holds every table and figure that is not in the
paper, with the same numbers.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Reading this edition.** This is the print edition of the online appendix. It holds every table and figure that is
not in the paper, numbered Table or Figure OA.*k*; where the site shows one of the paper's own exhibits beside them,
a line names it and the section of the paper that carries it. Where an exhibit exists under both calibrations of
the households' taste for leisure, the paper's calibration, common $X$, comes first and the alternative, vector
$X_i$ (OA.3.2), follows it. The site adds, for every exhibit, the value under the pointer, the link from a marker
of a figure to the table row that prints it, the switch between the two calibrations with the cells they differ
in marked, and the download of the files each exhibit reads.
:::

## Robustness at a glance {#robustness}

Figure G.1 of the paper, repeated here, sets its quantitative results against every specification the paper reports.
Each panel is one result: how the tax rate responds to the Bismarckian index $\theta$, to acute ageing and to France's income distribution and voting
patterns with the design given, and how the chosen design responds to the last three. Each marker is the same
result under one specification: the intertemporal elasticity of substitution (IES) $\rho$, the calibration of the
taste for leisure, the host economy, and for the chosen design the cost specification and the Frisch elasticity
$\xi$. Results are changes against the host's own baseline at the same IES, and the paper's own reading, the U.S.
under a common $X$ at an IES of one with the cost of section 7, is the highlighted marker. [Click a marker for the table that
prints it.]{.content-visible when-format="html"}
